overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to review executive session minutes at reasonable intervals, failing to take roll call votes in executive session, and keeping insufficient minutes, and found no violation on executive session purposes.

allegations.summary: Board routinely failed to review and approve executive session minutes in a timely manner.
allegations.key_passage: In other words, the Open Meeting Law does not require that a public body approve executive session minutes in a timely manner, but rather that the executive session minutes be “create[d] and maintain[ed]” and “review[ed]” “at reasonable intervals” to determine whether continued nondisclosure is warranted.

allegations.summary: Board failed to state the purpose for executive session; raised too late, as the failure occurred in open session.
allegations.key_passage: Because allegations 2, 4, 8, and 9 all concern matters that occurred, or should have occurred, in open session, we find that the complaint filed with the Board on January 12, 2024, concerning meetings that took place more than 30 days prior, is untimely as to those allegations and we decline to review them.

allegations.summary: Board entered executive session for purposes not permitted under G.L. c. 30A, § 21(a)(6) (real property), including on Oct. 19, 2022, Mar. 1 and Aug. 2, 2023.
allegations.key_passage: We are satisfied that the Board convened in executive session for a proper purpose on October 19 and that the discussions held in executive session were appropriately limited to the stated purpose.

allegations.summary: Chair failed to make appropriate declarations in open session before entering executive session; raised too late.
allegations.key_passage: Because allegations 2, 4, 8, and 9 all concern matters that occurred, or should have occurred, in open session, we find that the complaint filed with the Board on January 12, 2024, concerning meetings that took place more than 30 days prior, is untimely as to those allegations and we decline to review them.

allegations.summary: Board failed to periodically review executive session minutes at reasonable intervals to decide whether continued nondisclosure was warranted.
Executive session minutes were improperly redacted when released to the public.
allegations.key_passage: However, concerns about the propriety of redactions made in accordance with the Public Records Law should be directed to the Public Records Division in the Secretary of the Commonwealth’s Office.

allegations.summary: Board failed to vote by roll call while in executive session.
Minutes failed to state members present or absent; raised too late, as the omission arose in open session.
allegations.key_passage: Because allegations 2, 4, 8, and 9 all concern matters that occurred, or should have occurred, in open session, we find that the complaint filed with the Board on January 12, 2024, concerning meetings that took place more than 30 days prior, is untimely as to those allegations and we decline to review them.

allegations.summary: Chair failed to state whether the open meeting would resume after executive session; raised too late.
allegations.key_passage: Because allegations 2, 4, 8, and 9 all concern matters that occurred, or should have occurred, in open session, we find that the complaint filed with the Board on January 12, 2024, concerning meetings that took place more than 30 days prior, is untimely as to those allegations and we decline to review them.

allegations.summary: Executive session minutes failed to reference documents and materials used during the session.
allegations.key_passage: Finally, the Board acknowledges that minutes of its executive sessions failed to include a list of documents used during the executive session and, in some instances, failed to accurately record what occurred during the executive sessions.

allegations.summary: Board failed to keep accurate minutes of executive sessions.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.

Review minutes of all executive sessions held from 2020 to present not yet approved for release, to determine if continued non-disclosure is warranted, and certify compliance to the AG within 90 days.
remedy_passage: In addition, we order the Board to review minutes of all executive sessions held from 2020 to present that have not yet been approved for release to the public, to determine if continued non-disclosure is warranted.
